name: Tertius
overview: Tertius is a male figure noted in Scripture for his role as the scribe who wrote down the Apostle Paul's letter to the Romans. Beyond this unique contribution, there is no additional personal or tribal information recorded about him in the biblical text.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Tertius' appears only once in Scripture and carries no specified meaning or divine origin in the biblical record. It is simply presented as his proper name in Romans 16:22.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Tertius beyond his role as the scribe of Paul's letter to the Romans. There are no additional relational details provided.
scriptureSignificance: Tertius holds significance as the trusted amanuensis who faithfully transcribed Paul's epistle to the Romans, a foundational letter for Christian doctrine. His involvement underscores the collaborative efforts in the early church to preserve and communicate apostolic teaching accurately.
